As people ascend the corporate ladder, a dangerous illusion often takes root. It is easy to mistake a grand title, an executive boardroom seat, or a growing list of accolades for a license to dismiss others. In many traditional workplaces, we see leaders wrap themselves in the cold armor of ego, treating everyday interactions as transactional and creating a heavy atmosphere of silent anxiety. They become so insulated by their own metrics that they forget the human beings executing the vision. But status should never replace soul. YOU ARE NEVER TOO IMPORTANT TO BE KIND TO PEOPLE. True authority is never validated by how many people bow to your rank; it is measured by how beautifully you lift others up. It takes a profoundly secure mind and a kind heart to drop the pedestal and realize that every single individual—regardless of position—deserves radical respect. When you inject vibrant good energy into universal kindness, you construct an unshakeable sanctuary of deep trust and psychological safety. True high performance is unlocked only when people feel seen, valued, and protected by those at the top. Let your legacy be defined by your humility, not your hierarchy. Don't just lead a team; inspire a movement of humanity within your organization. Let kindness be the legacy you leave behind in every interaction. To master the soft skills that drive hard results, order copies of my book, The Blueprint of Leadership, for your entire team today, and lead with a legacy of kindness. Invest in your team’s growth. On Tuesday night Choose Creativity/Lulu & Leo Fund honored me with their Inspired Leadership Award at Tribeca Rooftop in New York City. Marina and Kevin Krim founded Choose Creativity after losing their two children, Lulu and Leo, in 2012. What they built from that loss is one of the most quietly extraordinary things I have ever encountered : a program that teaches thousands of children that they are creative, resilient, and capable of more than anyone has told them yet. I did not know this organization before they found me, and it has been very special to get to know their mission. Then Arianna Huffington took the stage to present my award. Arianna and I have many things in common from our Mediterranean origin, but when we first met years ago we immediately bonded over our shared love of Maria Callas. In her remarks, Arianna spoke about a particular kind of woman. The kind history keeps trying to contain. Too loud. Too passionate. Too big for whatever room she is standing in. The kind who spends years trying to make herself acceptable, until eventually she decides to stop shrinking to make others comfortable. And what follows is something the world wasn’t ready for but needed. Maria Callas was the perfect example of that type of woman. Arianna wrote Maria’s biography in 1977. She was 28 years old. A young Greek woman in London trying to understand another Mediterranean woman who had refused to be diminished by anyone or anything. She had no idea that decades later, in Indianapolis of all places, an Italian woman would pick up that book in one of the most difficult moments of her life and find herself in it. That Italian woman was me. And that’s what great creativity does: it reaches people you might never meet, in moments you cannot predict, and gives them exactly what they need. Arianna and I were connected through Maria before we ever met. Three Mediterranean women across a century. Same refusal. Same North. That’s why having Arianna presenting this award was such a full circle moment for me. And then I looked out at the audience. And saw so many of my colleagues, my teammates and my friends. People who have been deep in the work with me, on campaigns, on stages, in rooms where we tried to do things nobody had done before. I was so touched to see my team and my friends showing up in person to celebrate with me. Thank you Marina and Kevin. Thank you Choose Creativity. Thank you Arianna. And thank you to every person who showed up on Tuesday night to share this moment with me. ❤️

Prevenire non è un'opzione. È una responsabilità che riguarda tutti noi. È il messaggio che ho portato oggi sul palco della Milano Health Week, durante la Cerimonia di apertura della prima edizione del festival in Piazza Gae Aulenti, dedicato a prevenzione, innovazione e benessere. Ho scelto di partire dai numeri, perché aiutano a leggere il contesto: gli investimenti in salute variano da territorio a territorio e la crescita delle condizioni croniche ci invita a riportare la prevenzione al centro. Un impegno in cui credo profondamente, prima come persona e poi come azienda: perché mettere la prevenzione al centro significa rendere la salute più accessibile e vicina alla vita di ciascuno. Un privilegio essere parte di questo evento come speaker, e un grande onore per Lilly esserne main sponsor. Un altro passo nella direzione in cui crediamo: una salute più accessibile e personalizzata. #WeAreLilly #MilanoHealthWeek
linkedin_activity.text_en: Prevention is not an option. It is a responsibility that concerns all of us. This is the message I brought to the Milan Health Week stage today, during the Opening Ceremony of the first edition of the festival in Piazza Gae Aulenti, dedicated to prevention, innovation and well-being. I chose to start with the numbers, because they help to read the context: investments in health vary from territory to territory and the growth of chronic conditions invites us to bring prevention back to the centre. A commitment in which I believe deeply, first as a person and then as a company: because putting prevention at the centre means making health more accessible and closer to everyone's life. It is a privilege to be part of this event as a speaker, and a great honour for Lilly to be its main sponsor. Another step in the direction we believe in: more accessible and personalized health. #WeAreLilly #MilanoHealthWeek

linkedin_activity.text: Last week, I had the privilege of visiting the Lilly Australia & New Zealand team during Vivid Sydney , and what a backdrop it was. A city literally lit up with creativity and energy, and inside our walls, a team doing exactly the same. They took me through their work, their wins, and the road ahead. Among it all, the team hosted a Vivid Minds event “A New Horizon of Health”, which left a real impression. Australia's health system is facing the kind of pressures that demand honest, forward-looking conversation, and Lilly Australia created the space for exactly that. One theme came through clearly: Australians are still waiting too long to access new medicines – 712 days from medicine registration to reimbursement, and often years after they are available elsewhere. It’s a challenge that requires continued focus, collaboration, and a shared commitment to ensuring patients are not left behind when it comes to innovation. It felt particularly meaningful to experience all of this over our 150th anniversary. 150 years of putting patients first. 150 years of science, integrity, and innovation. That legacy shows up every day in the people who live it, and I saw plenty of that in Sydney. This is a team with genuine clarity of purpose and belief in the difference they are making for people every day. To everyone at Lilly Australia & New Zealand. I can’t wait to see what you do next. #WeAreLilly #Lilly150

I think this mindset has been clear from the beginning 150 years ago—from mass-producing insulin to AI and what it can unlock for patients. As @DiogoRau puts it: the patient is waiting. Last week, I had the opportunity to participate in Day 2 of four, "Conquer New Trails," at the NCAA Career in Sports Forum in Indianapolis. A huge thank you to Mark Trumbo , Christal Peterson, MBA , Ashley Jocelyn , and the entire NCAA Leadership Development team for creating an outstanding experience for more than 180 student-athletes from across the country. One question I asked the room was how many were visiting Indiana for the first time. Nearly every hand went up. Welcome to Indy! It was a privilege to introduce these future leaders to Indy, recently ranked the #3 Best Sports Business City in America by Sports Business Journal , and share how our region is working to connect talent to opportunity through initiatives like Accelerate Indy 2030. Programs like the Career in Sports Forum are a reminder that talent development doesn't happen by accident. It happens when businesses and professionals invest their time, share their experiences, and help open doors for the next generation. Special thanks to Matthew White , Lindsay Sparks , Matisse Lee, MBA , and the many mentors, speakers, and volunteers who made the experience so impactful. To every student-athlete who joined us last week, keep exploring, keep building connections, and keep blazing your own trail. And when it's time to launch your career, we'd love you to consider a Life In Indy .
